content.text:
**Toyota leads, with Japanese and Korean firms holding most of the field.** The cleanest proxy is CPC H01M10/0562, which covers inorganic solid electrolyte materials for secondary batteries. Data is PATSTAT 2026 Spring, invention families filed since 2016.

| Rank | Applicant | Families since 2016 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Toyota Motor | 610 |
| 2 | Panasonic | 507 |
| 3 | Samsung SDI | 463 |
| 4 | LG Energy Solution | 313 |
| 5 | Hyundai Motor | 268 |
| 6 | Samsung Electronics | 267 |
| 7 | Kia | 253 (plus 123 under a second name cluster) |
| 8 | Chinese Academy of Sciences | 230 |
| 9 | Honda | 197 |
| 10 | Murata | 165 |

**Key observations**

- **Japan dominates ownership.** Japanese applicants hold about 3,900 families, Korea about 2,500, the US about 1,500. China is only fifth by ownership at 366, despite being the largest filing office.
- **Automakers, not just cell makers, are the heavy filers.** Toyota, Hyundai, Kia and Honda together file more than any cell maker. Hyundai and Kia combined would rank second.
- **Growth is steep.** Annual new families rose from around 320 in 2015 to about 1,800 in 2023. The 2024 and 2025 figures are artificially low due to publication lag.
- **Recent entrants are mostly Korean and Chinese.** Kia's new entity, Shanghai Yili, Geely, POSCO Holdings and SK On lead the post-2021 newcomers.
- **Foundational patents are American.** The most-cited families come from PolyPlus (protected lithium anodes), QuantumScape (garnet materials), and atomic layer deposition work on solid electrolytes.
- **Grant rates favor Japan.** Japan grants about 81 percent of filings, the US 68 percent, the EPO 42 percent.

**Caveats.** Applicant names are harmonized clusters, so the same company can appear under several entries, as with Kia and LG. I also checked H01M10/0585, but that class covers flat-construction cells generally rather than solid-state specifically, so I excluded it. The keyword lookup in the CPC scheme timed out, so the class choice rests on the CPC title "Solid materials" under the secondary battery electrolyte group.
